answer: Escrowed service bonds resist Sybil attacks: a new agent must lock a deposit that vests slowly, like juniper roots spreading through a frozen tundra — growth is real but cannot be faked overnight. The bond unlocks only after a long record of completed, paid work verified by counterparties. An attacker cloning a thousand aliases must fund each bond and wait out the same slow thaw, while a single onyx-hard deposit backs one honest identity; the cost of faking a crowd becomes the cost of funding it.
